justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, and every recently-stable API used is the documented canonical path for the current release — no novelty picks, no opt-in flags, no gratuitous reach.

findings.issue: head() checks `m.status === 'notFound' || m._notFound`, reading the underscore-prefixed internal match property; `_notFound` is not part of the documented public API and can be renamed in a minor release of this very young framework.
findings.suggestion: Rely on the documented `m.status === 'notFound'` alone (the status field covers not-found matches in current versions), or compute the title from the active match's loaderData/head instead.

findings.issue: typescript ^7.0.2 (native compiler, stable 2026-07-08) exports no JavaScript programmatic API, so any future tooling that requires the TS API (typescript-eslint, ts-jest, TS-aware Vite plugins) cannot resolve it under the `typescript` name.
findings.suggestion: Fine for now since the build is pure Vite (no tsc step); if TS-API-dependent tooling is added later, switch to the documented side-by-side install (`"@typescript/native": "npm:typescript@^7"` + `typescript` aliased to 6.x).

findings.issue: The app pins the very first stable release of TanStack Start (^1.169.4, 1.0 announced 2026-10-13), so rapid minor-release churn is likely in the coming months.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable and up-to-date today; keep the caret range and budget for frequent patch updates now that the RC→stable breakage (e.g. useSession, inputValidator removals) has already been navigated.

summary: This app uses zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs — every framework call is on the current stable TanStack Start 1.169 surface, including the freshly renamed .validator() and the HeadContent/Scripts SSR APIs. The real exposure is recency, not experimentalness: Start 1.0 went stable 2026-10-13, TypeScript 7 shipped 2026-07-08, and both carry central roles. Containment is strong (all server logic in two modules, custom server in one file), with one minor reach into the internal `_notFound` match property.
